newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev rises amid low dollar demand.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev rises amid low dollar demand.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev strengthened to 225.00/80 per dollar from 226.50/227.60 at Tuesday's close in thin interbank trade as foreign currency supply topped demand, dealers said.
The dollar was bid between 224.00/90 levs and was offered between 225.70/226.50 around 1015 local time (0815 GMT).
"Dollars are sought only for meeting pending payments as banks and final clients channel free liquidity into high yield lev-denominated investments," another dealer said.
A record high main interest rate, in force for a week now, has started to alleviate pressure on the fragile national currency, traders said.

The lev weakened to 237 per dollar a week ago just before the central bank hiked its main rate to 25 percent monthly or 300 percent annually from 108 percent in a bid to restore confidence in the falling national currency. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
